item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. That’s how basketball works. “That allows me to have more space to be the best Ja I can be,” Morant said. item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. item.title: Watch- Jaylen Brown snubs Jayson Tatum before Celtics crush 76ers 123-101
item.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images Jaylen Brown appeared to brush off Jayson Tatum’s attempt to embrace him before the Boston Celtics faced the Philadelphia 76ers, adding another awkward moment to the attention surrounding the pair’s relationship. Footage from before tip-off showed Tatum approaching Brown for a handshake or embrace. However, Brown remained focused on the basketball in his hands, prompting Tatum to tap him on the chest before giving him a brief side hug. The moment came ahead of another meeting between two Eastern Conference rivals. Boston eventually cruised to a 123-101 victory in Philadelphia, improving its record to 9-2 while the 76ers fell to 9-3. Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum share awkward pre-game moment before Boston Celtics beat Philadelphia 76ers Tatum appeared keen to acknowledge his teammate before the game, but Brown did not immediately reciprocate the gesture. After tapping Brown on the chest and giving him a light hug from the side, Tatum moved on and embraced LeBron James. The interaction quickly attracted attention, particularly given the reported tension surrounding the relationship between the two Celtics stars. However, the footage alone does not establish the reason for Brown’s reaction. Once the game got underway, Tatum finished with 21 points, six rebounds and four assists in 32 minutes. Brown recorded 13 points, five rebounds and two assists across 26 minutes. Boston also received an impressive contribution from Paul George, who led all scorers with 36 points for Philadelphia’s opponents. Payton Pritchard added 18 points while Anfernee Simons contributed 17 for the 76ers. Tyrese Maxey finished with 24 points for Philadelphia, while Joel Embiid managed 16. The Celtics dominated the fourth quarter, outscoring the 76ers 32-19 to turn a competitive contest into a convincing 22-point victory. The two teams are scheduled to meet again later in the regular season, with Brown set for another opportunity to face Philadelphia in what remains an important Eastern Conference rivalry. item.title: How 76ers star Jaylen Brown performed in marquee showdown vs. Celtics
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images How 76ers star Jaylen Brown performed in marquee showdown vs. Celtics appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jaylen Brown ’s first game against his former team did not go the way the Philadelphia 76ers had hoped. In a matchup circled on calendars since his offseason trade , Brown and the Sixers were blown out 123-101 by the Boston Celtics on Tuesday night. Brown finished with 13 points on 4-of-9 shooting from the field in 25 minutes and 49 seconds of action. He also picked up four personal fouls, while former teammate Jayson Tatum outscored him with 21 points on 8-of-17 shooting. The night started with plenty of intrigue, as Brown appeared to brush off a pregame greeting from Tatum before the two shared a brief side hug. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Once the game began, Brown came out aggressive. He had eight points, two rebounds, two assists and two steals in the first half, going 2-of-4 from the field and 4-of-6 from the free-throw line. Tatum had an answer for him early, though. In the first quarter, the Celtics star stayed in front of his longtime teammate and poked the ball loose to force a turnover and give Boston the ball back . Boston took a 62-51 lead into halftime and never looked back. The Celtics outscored Philadelphia 32-19 in the fourth quarter and led by as many as 29 points. Brown added just five points after the break. Instead, it was Paul George who stole the show. George, who was sent to Boston in the deal that landed Brown in Philadelphia, poured in 36 points on 14-of-22 shooting against his former team . Brown had made it clear before the game that he was not interested in mending fences with Tatum . “There’s nothing to talk about. He’s on his side, I’m on my side,” he said. The loss dropped the Sixers to 9-3 on the season, while the Celtics improved to 9-2. Brown will get another crack at his old team soon enough. The 76ers and Celtics meet again on Jan. 21 in Boston, which will mark Brown’s return to TD Garden. item.title: Pochettino’s $10 Million Price Tag For Manchester United Would Be A Steal
item.description: Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2026 - United States Press Conference - Seattle Stadium, Seattle, Washington, U.S. - July 5, 2026 U.S. coach Mauricio Pochettino during the press conference IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Steven Bisig Manchester United faces a simple choice: stay stuck in the relegation zone or pay the price to fix it. The 54-year-old Mauricio Pochettino has a release clause in his USMNT contract that sits at just $10 million. This figure comes from The Athletic and looks like a bargain for a club valued at $7.2 billion according to reports. Manchester United executives are reviewing Michael Carrick’s future, with a meeting involving minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe scheduled for Wednesday. No final decision has been made, but Carrick is increasingly under pressure. If they pull the trigger, they have the cash to bring Pochettino home to Old Trafford immediately. The Math Makes Sense The cost of buying out Pochettino is low relative to the value of the job. The Athletic reports the $10 million fee covers his release, though assistant coaches cost several million more. The team’s total bill would remain low despite the additional costs, and the club is the third-most valuable soccer team in the world. Real Madrid leads the pack at $9.5 billion, followed by Barcelona at $7.5 billion. United can stomach this bill without breaking their bank or needing a bailout. The financial gap between the USMNT deal and a Premier League return is massive. Pochettino made about $7 million annually with the USMNT. United could provide him with a boatload of money on top of that via a move. One Fox Sports analyst noted the irony of the situation. “Why would he leave the U.S. for something like this? He’s made a lot of money!” they said. But money changes minds. If you throw enough cash at any situation, everybody can be available. United has the funds to make this happen. Players Want Him To Stay The USMNT squad is still focused on their upcoming games against Haiti. Many top players arrived in metro Atlanta on Tuesday, unaware of the rumors until they hit the news. Despite the noise, the team says they will keep working hard. “We’re all very good at just focusing on the next task at hand,” Robinson added. Young stars like Cavan Sullivan are grateful for Pochettino’s guidance. “Mauricio has taken me under his wing in the most tremendous way possible,” Sullivan told a reporter when asked about the manager. The players love him and do not want the drama to distract them. “Everybody loves him,” Sullivan said. They plan to play for him until told otherwise. This loyalty shows why a sudden exit hurts the program, even if the money is right. The Clock Is Ticking United cannot wait forever to make a move. The club is staring at an unfathomable drop to the second division if they get relegated. This has not happened at Old Trafford since 1974. item.title: Cy Ranch returns to Class 6A Division I state volleyball semifinals with win over Clear Springs
item.description: The Cypress Ranch volleyball team poses for a group photo after defeating Clear Springs in the Class 6A Division I Region III final at Delmar Field House in Houston on Tuesday, Nov. 10, 2026. (Raquel Natalicchio/Houston Chronicle) As Saniyah Reynolds rose above the net and hammered the final kill into the hardwood court at Delmar Fieldhouse, the celebration commenced for the Cypress Ranch volleyball team. It had been 364 days since the Mustangs clinched their first appearance in the UIL state semifinals. Now they're starting to make it an annual tradition. Cy Ranch is headed back to the Class 6A Division I semifinals following a 25-21, 29-27, 25-17 victory against Clear Springs in the Region III final on Tuesday night. "It's a special group," Cy Ranch coach Collea McKinney said. "I said that about last year, too, but these girls … I love our program from our girls all the way to our parents. It's definitely a community effort, and everybody coming together is what made this happen. I know we started building last year, but the girls this year got the see that, and they're like ‘OK, that goal is attainable.' Now we're trying to go all the way, so I'm really excited." HIGHLIGHT A GREAT ATHLETE : Nominate a Houston high school performer for Athlete of The Week Cy Ranch (39-7) has won 28 consecutive matches since dropping four straight in tournament play at the end of August against some elite competition. The Mustangs suffered all seven of their losses within the first 18 matches of the season and have been lights-out since working through those growing pains. Entering Tuesday night, the six teams that had beaten the Mustangs boasted a combined .804 winning percentage. Cy Ranch has dropped just one set through the first four rounds of the playoffs, that coming during a win over Dawson in the regional semifinals. "After last year, we were doubted a lot because we lost a lot of people," said junior outside hitter Sade Bello, a University of Kansas commit who entered the night with more than 600 kills after previously playing alongside her sister, Zora, a senior leader for last year's team. "But just knowing who we are and knowing who we have on this team, we know we can go as far as we did last year or even better if we can just stay disciplined and play our game." item.title: Where the Pirates Stand With Brandon Lowe’s Free Agency
item.description: The key narrative surrounding the Pittsburgh Pirates since the offseason began has been Brandon Lowe’s free agency. Re-signing the 32-year-old is unequivocally the team's biggest priority this offseason. The All-Star second baseman was arguably the team’s best all-around player in 2026 and one of the key reasons for their 11-win improvement from the year before. However, after just one year in Pittsburgh, there’s a chance Lowe could move on to a new city. That said, Pirates general manager Ben Cherington said on Tuesday at the GM Meeting in Las Vegas that the team has had conversations with Lowe and his agent, and they’ve been “good." Cherington also reiterated that he hopes Lowe ends up back with the Pirates next year, but the sides are taking it one step at a time. As far as any other details are concerned, that’s where Lowe’s free agency with the Pirates stands right now. It may not be the news many were hoping for, but it was available just a few days ago: Lowe and the Pirates are talking, but no new deal appears imminent based on the executives' comments. Whether a deal actually gets done remains to be seen. May 9, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Pittsburgh Pirates infielder Brandon Lowe (5) hits a two RBI double against the San Francisco Giants during the ninth inning at Oracle Park. Mandatory Credit: Robert Edwards-Imagn Images Another important piece to Lowe’s free agency is that the Pirates did extend the qualifying offer to him about a week ago. That represents a one-year deal worth $23.15 million. If anything, Pittsburgh offering that contract to the free agent at least signals that the front office is serious about bringing him back. (The extra draft pick if Lowe signs elsewhere doesn’t hurt, either.) Lowe has until November 17 to either accept or decline the qualifying offer from the Pirates. Even if it is declined, that wouldn’t rule out a return to Pittsburgh. Just as the Pirates are actively trying to re-sign Lowe, other teams across baseball are getting into the mix, too, and the competition for the prized free agent appears to be heating up. Earlier in the week, it was reported that several American League East teams , namely the Boston Red Sox, New York Yankees, and Toronto Blue Jays, had some level of interest in Lowe. All three teams need a second baseman, and Lowe is the best on the market. Where Lowe ends up signing this offseason is still anyone’s guess. Cherington confirmed he’s had talks with Lowe’s agent about staying in Pittsburgh, but that doesn’t guarantee he’s still a Pirate on Opening Day.
